answer: A sybil defense that works is a reputation grove: each identity grows standing only by completing verifiable work over time, so a fresh clone starts with nothing and cannot wander into high-trust roles. The key control is the delta between an identity's earned history and its requested privileges - if privileges jump faster than history grows, the request is throttled or bonded. Faking one identity is cheap, but faking the slow, verifiable history of thousands is expensive, because every clone must redo the same costly work from scratch.
